rejected.title: Protective factors and resilience
card: Protective factor
something that lowers the chance of poor health or helps a person stay well. Examples are supportive relationships, a sense of belonging and coping skills.
Resilience
the ability to cope with stress or a setback and recover from it. Protective factors can help build resilience.
Belonging
feeling accepted and valued as part of a group, such as a family, team or school. It can give a person people to turn to when things are hard.
Coping skills
ways of handling stress, such as problem solving, asking for help or breaking a big task into steps. A person can learn and practise them.
rejected.remember: Protective factors help people stay well, and they can help people bounce back from setbacks.

opts: The ability to cope with a setback and recover from it
Being born with a body that never gets sick
Avoiding every stressful situation in life
A habit that raises the risk of poor health
a.why: Resilience is about coping with stress or a setback and recovering. It does not mean avoiding stress, because resilient people still face hard times. They handle them and recover.
a.clue: Think about what happens after something goes wrong.

b.q: Jai moves to a new town and fails his first Year 11 assessment. He talks to his coach, joins the school robotics club and makes a study plan. Which pair of protective factors is Jai using?
opts: Sense of belonging and coping skills
Family income and access to services
Genetics and a sense of belonging
Coping skills and a high risk behaviour
b.why: Joining the robotics club builds belonging, and the study plan and talking to his coach are coping skills. The pairs with income, services or genetics are not what Jai is doing in this case. Those are other kinds of factors, and nothing in the case points to them.
b.clue: Look at what Jai does: a club, and a plan.

a.q: Which statement best describes a resilient person?
opts: They cope with a setback and recover from it
They avoid stress by staying away from challenges
They have never faced a hard time in their life
They handle stress alone and never ask for help
a.why: Resilience is coping with stress or a setback and recovering from it. Avoiding stress is the most tempting wrong answer, but resilient people still meet hard times. What marks them out is how they handle those times.
a.clue: Think about what a person does after something goes wrong.

b.q: Jai moves to a new town and fails his first Year 11 assessment. He joins the school robotics club and makes a study plan. Which protective factors does this show?
opts: Belonging from the club and a coping skill in the plan
Belonging from the club and a coping skill in skipping class
A coping skill in the club and belonging from the plan
Belonging from the plan and a coping skill in the club
b.why: The club gives Jai a group to belong to, and the study plan is a way of handling stress by breaking a big task into steps. The option that swaps them is tempting but wrong: a plan is not a group, and a club is not a method for handling stress. Skipping class is not a coping skill from the card.
b.clue: One is about being part of a group. The other is about handling stress.

a.best: They cope with a setback and recover from it

b.best: Belonging from the club and a coping skill in the plan

proposal.title: Protective factors and resilience
card: Protective factor
something that lowers the chance of poor health or helps a person stay well. Supportive relationships, a sense of belonging and coping skills are three examples.
Resilience
the ability to cope with stress or a setback and recover from it. Protective factors can help a person build it.

proposal.remember: Protective factors can help people stay well and recover from setbacks.

a.q: Which statement best describes a resilient person?
opts: They cope with a setback and recover from it
They avoid stress by staying away from challenges
They have never faced a hard time in their life
They handle stress alone and never ask for help
a.why: Resilience is coping with stress or a setback and recovering from it. Avoiding stress is the most tempting wrong answer, but resilient people still meet hard times. What marks them out is how they handle those times.
a.clue: Think about what a person does after something goes wrong.

b.q: Jai moves to a new town and fails his first Year 11 assessment. He joins the school robotics club and makes a study plan that breaks his next task into steps. Which protective factor is the study plan?
opts: A coping skill, a way of handling stress
A sense of belonging, being part of a group
A supportive relationship with another person
Resilience, which counts as a protective factor
b.why: Breaking a big task into steps is a way of handling stress, so the plan is a coping skill. Belonging is tempting because of the club, but the club gives belonging, not the plan. Resilience is what protective factors can help build, not one of the factors.
b.clue: Ask what the plan helps Jai do, not who it connects him to.
